metrics.name: Largest economy: export/GDP share
metrics.note: KEY: giants export BELOW their weight

metrics.name: Landlocked trade penalty
metrics.note: landlocked states trade ~30% less on Earth

metrics.name: 99th percentile trade / GDP
metrics.note: constrains the TAIL. Earth's most open economies (Hong Kong, Singapore, Luxembourg) reach 3-4x GDP; nothing previously stopped a country at 17x

metrics.name: Most open economy, trade / GDP
metrics.note: the single most extreme country in the world

metrics.name: Intra-continent share of world trade
metrics.note: Earth 2015 ~57% (Europe 68%, Asia 58%, Africa 18%). Tracks whether partners are too regional

metrics.name: Mean distance per unit of exports (km)
metrics.note: Earth 2015 ~4,900 km. Too low means distance decay is overwhelming the basket match

metrics.name: Top partner on another continent
metrics.note: Earth ~50%: China is largest partner across four continents. Near zero means each continent has collapsed onto its own resident giant

metrics.name: Biggest customer is not biggest supplier
metrics.note: Earth ~45%: Japan sells to the US and buys from China. Near zero means the big exporters are interchangeable and only distance is choosing between them

metrics.name: Bilateral imbalance, median pair
metrics.note: Earth: US-China 0.65, a typical pair 0.25-0.40. Low means no pair runs a structural surplus with another, only each country against the world

metrics.name: Median domestic value added in exports
metrics.note: Earth: Singapore 42%, Mexico 55%, Korea 63%, Germany 73%, China 83%, US 88%. Nobody reaches 100%: every country buys inputs. 167 of 172 sat at exactly 100% before the intermediate-goods layer existed
